claims.text: The initial alloy is as-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr suffers rapid internal oxidation because of poor oxygen resistance.
The intervention is deposition of an approximately 100–200 nm Al2O3 coating by atomic layer deposition.
ALD will produce a continuous, adherent, defect-free Al2O3 layer on HfNbTaTiZr.
The Al2O3 layer will act as a stable barrier to oxygen diffusion at 1000 °C.
ALD-deposited Al2O3 is inert and thermodynamically stable under the proposed high-temperature conditions.
The Al2O3 coating will prevent oxygen from penetrating the underlying alloy microstructure.
Preventing oxygen penetration will preserve the alloy's phase stability.
Preserving phase stability will preserve the alloy's mechanical properties.
After 100 hours in air at 1000 °C, coated specimens will exhibit significantly less oxygen uptake than uncoated specimens.
After 100 hours in air at 1000 °C, coated specimens will exhibit minimal oxide-scale growth.
The coating will allow the alloy to retain 8–16% room-temperature ductility after high-temperature exposure.
The coating will allow the alloy to retain a high-temperature yield strength of 163–530 MPa.
Rapid oxidation of uncoated HfNbTaTiZr causes degradation of its mechanical performance.
Coating spallation induced by extreme thermal cycling may diminish the protective effect.

contradictions.description: The conditions field implies that coated and uncoated specimens are exposed at 1000 °C under strain-rate-controlled mechanical loading, whereas the experiment design describes an unloaded 100-hour exposure followed by tensile testing.
